text:
carmen: noticed p95 jump on canary v2.7.0 at 50% in us-east, started ~10m ago :warning:
deploy-bot: rollout v2.7.0 -> 50% us-east. snapshot p95=920ms (baseline 390ms), errors=0.2%. autorevert rule p95>750ms sustained 5m. breach detected 6m ago.
ben: that's past the auto threshold, will it auto-revert?
deploy-bot: autopilot scheduled auto-revert in 0m30s unless suppressed.
lina: recommend manual hold. traffic still healthy and failures minimal; we can triage without an immediate rollback.
ops-raf: agree. pin traffic and do targeted pod restarts + diag scripts. we should prepare rollback notes in case.
carmen: pinning now and applying manual hold. deploy-bot: traffic pinned at 50% by carmen; autopilot suppressed.
infra-zoe: ran diag, seeing kernel fallback at sequence boundary ~256 on 3 pods. looks like kernel selection flapping.
ben: if kernel flapping, rollback to v2.6.9 (build 20260430.5) is safest. hotfix might be riskier during traffic.
pm-jo: if we rollback, what's the customer comm wording? suggest: "Paused canary for v2.7.0 due to increased latency in a subset of traffic; investigating."
ops-raf: prep customer blurb and tag support; don't send until we decide.
carmen: plan: try restarts on the three affected pods, wait 4m. if cluster p95 stays >650ms for 5m, execute rollback to v2.6.9. logging action.
sre-bot: metric update: pod-22 p95 down to 480ms after restart; pod-24 still 860ms; cluster p95 710ms.
infra-zoe: restarting pod-24 now.
sre-bot: pod-24 p95 dropped to 430ms after restart; cluster p95 460ms.
carmen: good recovery. keep manual hold for 12m. rollback threshold remains 5m sustained >650ms. ops-raf please send customer blurb now and tag support watch.
ops-raf: sent customer note and created watch. recorded decision: reason=canary-p95-drift, action=manual-hold+pod-restarts, rollback-if=5m sustained >650ms, rollback-target=v2.6.9
ben: documenting rollback block in release notes until postmortem complete.
carmen: thanks all, will update thread if it re-escalates. :hourglass:
